theme: Bitcoin tests the $80K cost basis of ETFs and treasuries as SpaceX borrows $40B, AI stocks slide, and oil spikes.

items.tab: 12 ETF vs company BTC cost basis
items.title: Bitcoin price vs what ETFs and public companies paid
items.picked: Bitcoin is testing $80,000 this weekend after getting rejected near $85,000, and the most-shared posts point out that corporate treasuries and US spot ETFs paid roughly that much on average. This chart plots the price against both groups' average cost.
items.matters: When the price sits on the big holders' cost basis, their whole position is roughly break-even, so this is the level where 'underwater treasuries' headlines start and where dip buyers tend to show up.
items.know: As of Oct 14 (BTC $81,562) the sheet has US spot ETFs at a $76,645 average cost on 1.30M BTC and public companies at $78,881 on 1.30M BTC, a price-to-cost ratio of 1.06 and 1.03. Those are lower than the $80K-$81.5K figures in today's X posts, which use different methods, and the data is weekly and ends Oct 14.

items.title: Borrowing for AI: total debt at Big Tech and CoreWeave
items.picked: SpaceX is closing a $40B debt package led by Apollo and Goldman at around 7.75% to 8.3%, more than a point above its existing bonds, as lenders charge more for AI spending. This chart shows how fast the other big AI spenders have been borrowing.
items.matters: Debt, not just cash flow, is now funding the AI build-out, and rising borrowing costs are what's behind the AI credit-risk worries on X this week.
items.know: In the latest quarter (Jun 2026) the sheet has Amazon at $133.0B of debt, Oracle $129.5B, Alphabet $101.1B, Meta $83.7B, Microsoft $40.3B and CoreWeave $35.6B. Alphabet roughly doubled from $49.1B at FY 2025 and Amazon from $68.8B, while Microsoft's debt fell. SpaceX isn't in this tab, and the data stops at June, before the September-quarter filings.

items.title: SPCX price-to-sales since the June IPO
items.picked: SpaceX's new filing is the talk of X: net income topped $4B in the quarter, helped by a $561M paper gain on its Boring Company stake, and it's lining up a $40B loan. This chart shows what investors pay for each dollar of SpaceX revenue.
items.matters: Even after the selloff, SPCX trades at a sales multiple far above almost any large company, so every earnings line and merger headline gets measured against that price.
items.know: On Oct 20 the sheet has SPCX at $147.79, a $1,948B market cap and 84.6x trailing revenue of $23.04B, down from 109.9x on IPO day (Jun 12) and a peak of 144.4x on Jun 16. The data ends Oct 20, so it misses Thursday's roughly 9% drop, and check whether the $23.04B revenue input includes the new quarter before quoting the multiple.

items.title: Neocloud stocks in 2026 (Dec 31, 2025 = 100)
items.picked: Nebius is down more than 30% this month and IREN is back near its 2021 IPO price, even as executives say capacity is sold out and Nvidia's Jensen Huang says demand will solve their funding needs. This chart shows how far each neocloud has swung this year.
items.matters: These stocks are the most leveraged way to trade AI demand, so their drop is a quick read on how worried the market is about debt-funded data center growth.
items.know: As of the Oct 16 close, the sheet has Nebius up 98% for the year, TeraWulf up 2%, CoreWeave down 14%, Applied Digital down 26%, IREN down 29% and Cipher down 39%. Nebius was up as much as 236% (index 335.6 on Jun 17). The data ends Oct 16, so this week's further drop isn't in it, and prices come from Yahoo Finance.

items.title: Nvidia valuation: price-to-sales and trailing P/E
items.picked: Nvidia has slid about 12% over the past dozen sessions to around $211, and traders on X are watching $200 as the next support. This chart shows how expensive the stock is relative to its sales and earnings.
items.matters: It answers the reply-guy claim that Nvidia is a bubble: the stock has fallen and earnings have grown, so the valuation is the cheapest it's been in years.
items.know: At the October 2026 reading, Nvidia's trailing P/E is 27.0x, the lowest of any month in the sheet going back to June 2019, and price-to-sales is 17.2x. Both peaked in July 2023 at 242.8x and 45.0x. These are month-end values, October's is partial, and the P/E is trailing, not forward.

items.title: S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 vs their 200-day averages
items.picked: The S&P 500 is within about 2% of its record, but a Kobeissi Letter post that 59% of its stocks are down 20% or more is trending, and the Nasdaq just had its worst day since June. This chart shows how stretched the two indexes are versus their long-term trend.
items.matters: Distance from the 200-day average is a simple gauge of how much room a selloff has before the trend breaks, and a narrowing gap shows momentum fading.
items.know: On Oct 16 the S&P 500 was 5.3% above its 200-day average and the Nasdaq-100 5.2% above, down from 7.7% and 11.8% a week earlier. The Nasdaq-100 gap was 12.1% on Oct 2. The data is weekly and ends Oct 16, so it misses this week's tech selloff, and the 59% breadth figure comes from the X post, not this tab.

items.title: Oil in today's dollars (WTI, inflation-adjusted)
items.picked: Oil jumped Friday after Houthi strikes in Saudi Arabia, with Brent settling at $116.72 and WTI at $103.27, the highest since April, and the Dow fell 653 points. This chart puts WTI in inflation-adjusted terms.
items.matters: Oil is feeding straight into the inflation and Fed debate, and the real price shows whether today's level is truly extreme or just high in nominal terms.
items.know: The sheet's latest monthly WTI average is $97.31 for September 2026 ($96.68 in August 2026 dollars), after $102.13 in May. In real terms that's below June 2022's $130.09 and far below the June 2008 record of $205.71. The data is monthly and stops at September, so October's spike isn't in it.

items.title: Texas robotaxi registrations: Tesla vs Waymo and others
items.picked: New Texas DMV filings show Tesla registered 69 more Cybercabs, and Tesla expanded its Austin robotaxi zone to the Grand Prix track area this weekend. This chart compares registered robotaxi fleets in Texas.
items.matters: Fleet size is the cleanest public scoreboard in the Tesla-vs-Waymo robotaxi race, and Cybercabs show Tesla shifting from Model Ys to its purpose-built vehicle.
items.know: As of the sheet's Oct 11 check, Tesla had 739 vehicles registered (420 Model Y and 319 Cybercabs), against Waymo's 1,185, Avride's 344 and Zoox's 63. That's stale: today's posts put Tesla at 420 Cybercabs out of 927. These are registrations, not active vehicles, and the registry doesn't say which city they run in.

items.title: Strategy: bitcoin per diluted share vs share count
items.picked: Michael Saylor is making the rounds saying bitcoin per share is Strategy's north star, and Strategy says it now holds 848,517 BTC after another small buy. This chart tracks how many sats each diluted share owns.
items.matters: Bitcoin per share is what MSTR holders actually own, so it shows whether selling new shares to buy bitcoin is adding to or diluting each holder's stake.
items.know: On Oct 12 the sheet has 187,750 sats per diluted share on 451.8M assumed diluted shares and 848,250 BTC. That's below the 220,429 peak on Jun 1, as the share count rose from 382.8M while holdings barely grew, but up from 158,827 in January 2025. The tab ends Oct 12, and diluted shares are an estimate.

items.title: Who holds the 20.1M bitcoin
items.picked: The White House is pushing ahead on a strategic bitcoin reserve built from the roughly 328,000 BTC the US already holds, and CME just posted record bitcoin futures volume. This chart shows how the supply splits among exchanges, ETFs, companies and governments.
items.matters: It puts the government reserve in context next to the ETFs and corporate treasuries that have absorbed so much of the supply since 2024.
items.know: As of Oct 14 the sheet has 2.68M BTC on exchanges, 1.30M in US spot ETFs, 1.30M at public companies, 0.60M with governments (US 328,372 as read Oct 11) and an estimated 1.1M for Satoshi, out of 20.1M. The government split is only in the latest row, and Satoshi's coins are an estimate, not a known wallet.
